labels.label: lem:elem
labels.notes: Yamabe.lem_elem : ∀ {q : ℝ}, 2 ≤ q → ∃ c, ∀ x, -1 ≤ x → (1 + x) ^ q ≤ 1 + q * x + c * (x ^ 2 + |x| ^ q). Read against l.673–677, hypothesis by hypothesis: q real with q ≥ 2 (the paper applies it at the non-integer q = p*), one c for all x ≥ −1 (∃ before ∀, as « there is c_q < ∞ with … for all x ≥ −1 »), and c real, so finite. (1 + x)^q and |x|^q are Real.rpow on a nonnegative base, and x ^ 2 is the monoid square (checked by rfl in a probe). This is exactly the printed statement. It has no sorry, standard axioms, and the witness elemC q = q²·2^q (elem_elemC) is kernel-checked, so the mark ``**`lem:elem`**`` is legitimate. The finding « printed without proof » is true: \end{lemma} is at l.677 and prop:starN begins at l.679. Extras, also sorry-free: elem_const_nonneg (every admissible c is ≥ 0, from x = 1 and Bernoulli) and elem_signed (max c q works for every real x, with |1+x|^q). The ledger row (nl_status open, no decls) is consistent with a first formalization.

labels.label: prop:starN
labels.notes: Unmarked and partial. That is correct and conservative. Yamabe.MeasuredModel.prop_starN carries hN : 3 ≤ N, [IsFiniteMeasure (M.vol g)], hD (a.e.-strong measurability), hl1 : 0 < M.lambda1 g, hCsp : ∃ C, M.IsSobolevPoincareConst g C, and hc (c is any constant satisfying lem:elem at q = pStar N). Leaving aside hN and hc, which are the label's own parameters, these are exactly thm_star3_corrected's hypotheses (Star3.lean:994–997, compared through #check). Conclusion 1 is the printed deficit bound at λ₁ = M.lambda1 g and C_SP = M.Csp g, for every u with u ≥ 0 and (eLpNorm …).toReal = 1. Since toReal ∞ = 0, the normalization means ‖u‖_q = 1. D = 1 − t², t = V^{1/q}ū, X = √dirichlet. t^{2−q} is an rpow on t > 0 (mean_pos_of_nonneg), so no junk value enters. Conclusion 2 is M.StarIneq g (starNAtil q c V λ₁ C_SP), which is eq:star for every u ≥ 0 at a genuine real infimum: the admissible set is nonempty at (1, 1/2) and bounded below by 0. So Lean ≥ paper, on the existential reading of « an explicit Ã » as well. The Ã of record is a reading (starNAtil: thm:star3's three branches with prop:starN's bound in case (ii), X₀ > 0, t₀ ∈ (0,1), min read as inf). It is disclosed in the checklist, in SCOPE and as a question. The « no cap » claim is checked by hand and in Lean. prop:starN's bound uses ‖v‖_q ≤ C_SP X with no min{·, 2}. For X < X₀ and t ≥ t₀ > 0 one has X^q = X^{q−2}X² ≤ X₀^{q−2}X², and t^{2−q} ≤ t₀^{2−q} because 2 − q < 0, so case (ii) is monotone. starN_split proves the three cases with no cap. The planner's [r] holds. The carried λ₁ > 0 and finite C_SP are OQ-109's readings, recorded there, and are the reason the row is not marked. The witness toy_prop_starN shows every hypothesis satisfiable together at N = 3. There is no witness for N ≥ 4, but nothing in the hypotheses depends on N beyond the exponent p* (note only). Minor: u ≥ 0 is read pointwise on the representative (∀ x, 0 ≤ M.val u x), while the paper's u ∈ W^{1,2} has u ≥ 0 a.e. This is the convention of the strict StarIneq, and the signed forms cover eq:star for every u. The checklist calls it « ✓ carried » (see findings).

findings.what: Part of this finding is wrong as stated. The optimal c_6 ≈ 31.37 at x ≈ 0.76 is confirmed. The thm:star3 corrected minima 1.070, 1.509, 2.508, 4.682 agree with a grid recomputation (1.070, 1.510, 2.509, 4.687). But the quoted infima of starNAtil are coarse-grid upper bounds, not the infima. At V = 1, λ₁ = 4π², c = c_6^opt they are ≈ 1.48, 2.45, 4.94, 11.04 at C_SP = 0.539, 0.70, 1.0, 1.5, against the claimed 1.50, 2.52, 5.17, 11.1 (4.6% high at C_SP = 1.0). At c = 2304 they are ≈ 19.54, 19.91, 23.11, 37.97, against « about 19.6 to 39 ». The conclusion holds: the general-N route is weaker than thm:star3's at N = 3. The audit verified this by a direct grid with local refinement; branch balance at C_SP = 0.539 is 1/X₀² ≈ C²/(1−t₀)² ≈ branch (ii) ≈ 1.48 at (X₀, t₀) ≈ (0.822, 0.557).
findings.fix: Replace the numbers by ≈ 1.48, 2.45, 4.94, 11.0 (and ≈ 19.5–38.0 at c_6 = 2304), or present them as upper bounds (« at most »), before the finding goes to the author.

findings.what: u ≥ 0 is read pointwise on the model's representative (∀ x, 0 ≤ M.val u x), while for u ∈ W^{1,2} the paper's u ≥ 0 means almost everywhere. This is the convention of the strict StarIneq (Star3.lean:812), and the signed forms (prop_starN_signed, starN_signed_of_consts) give eq:star for every u, so the eq:star conclusion is unaffected. Only the deficit-bound conjunct is narrower, by null sets, for a representative that is negative on a null set. It is disclosed in form: the REPORT shows the Lean hypothesis and the row is partial. But the checklist says « ✓ carried » where it is a reading.
